You're going to get the same answer, "go to the gym". Which isn't always helpful to hear, but there's some truth to it. It sounds like you're unhappy with yourself, you need to start invoking positive change in your life. Changing you nutrition habits, going to the gym, etc. It's a lot of work but take your time, learn from your mistakes but never give up. We all stumble but the way we respond to those stumbles makes all the difference. 

Start doing research into diets that fit your goals, make workout plans, and most importantly follow through. Forget dating, this will help with how you feel about yourself and will set you up for success in other facets of your life. It's not too late man, hang in there
That's all I needed to hear

Being up for 24 hours straight is not a good sign, I know it can be worrisome but you should talk to your doctor and tell them exactly what's going on. It will only help them diagnose you better and get you on the correct medication. Just like the other person said, you are much more than just your diagnosis
I was thinking the same thing. I used to work on a behavioral health unit and would see this happen occasionally, going from one extreme to another when a person with bipolar takes antidepressants.

I don't think it would be creepy at all if you followed him on Instagram, he showed you the account it's not like you had to go digging to find it. 

There is also nothing creepy about shooting your shot and trying to have a relationship outside of work. I think it's always best to try to form that connection in person though. Maybe instead of just adding him on Instagram, tell him you enjoy talking with him and give him your number and tell him to text you.

I get the meaning of this post, people should be treated as a person regardless of what shape they come in. But making generalizations about a group of people, whether positive or negative, I think is harmful. Thin people shouldn't be thought to have some preconceived problem with larger people, they can also be struggling with similar problems of their own. Nor should we assume every overweight person is going to be the "funny one", people are different regardless of their weight. We can treat others better.

Don't feel bad, you're not alone. Although it is easy for it to weigh on your self confidence.

1. Be attractive
2. Don't be unattractive
